clue.text: Rock music getting gold say

definitions.meaning: a loud, hard-driving genre of rock
gold is one example of a dense metallic element

explanation.definitionFit: The rock genre and the class of dense elements (lead, gold, mercury) share the same two-word name.

clue.text: Peak, or peaky under second in charge

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places this piece below the one before
second in tells us to take the second letter of the word charge

parts.note: peaky is British informal for looking pale and unwell

explanation.surface: A deputy commander is looking rather pale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second in charge' looks like a deputy but gives H, the second letter of 'charge'; 'under' puts ILL below it in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hill rises to a summit, a raised point of land.

clue.text: When somebody crosses one, that's slander

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left

indicators.note: crosses here means goes across and spans, so one word straddles the other

parts.note: a person is somebody
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Crossing somebody leads to them spreading malicious talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Casting aspersions means making damaging remarks about someone's character.

clue.text: Give up? Listen to why that is located outside

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'Give up? Listen to why that is located outside'. Y (sounds like why) + IE (that is) leaves LD, which 'located outside' does not supply; the clue appears misread in OCR and no source gives the printed text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Give up? Listen to why that is located outside

clue.text: Colour red mixed with lame embroidery

indicators.note: mixed with means the letters of the two words are blended together and rearranged

explanation.surface: Red thread combined with metallic lame fabric in some needlework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embroidery' completes the needlework picture and works as a second hint that the letters are worked into a pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: Emerald is a bright green shade, named after the gemstone.

clue.text: Old canine replaced by hearty dentist

indicators.note: replaced means the letters of canine are put back in a different order
hearty means take the heart, the central letter, of dentist

explanation.surface: A dentist with plenty of heart replaces a patient's canine tooth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canine' looks like a tooth for the dentist but is anagram fodder; T is the middle letter of DENTIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient means very old, from the distant past.

clue.text: English film that's short but heroic

parts.note: pic is a short, informal word for a picture, i.e. a film

explanation.surface: A brief English movie that is nonetheless grand and heroic.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic tale is on a heroic scale, celebrating legendary deeds.

clue.text: Clear strategy one adopted

indicators.note: adopted means taken in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a plan is a strategy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A clear-cut strategy is chosen by one person.
explanation.definitionFit: Something plain is obvious and easy to understand.

clue.text: Mark of distinction, to wit, plastic

parts.note: a credit is a grade awarded for good work in an exam
a card is a witty or amusing person

explanation.surface: A distinction, as it were, earned in some plastic subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to wit' looks like the stock phrase meaning namely, but 'wit' alone gives CARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic is slang for bank cards used for buying on account.

clue.text: Not enthusiastic about hot-gospeller physician at first

indicators.note: at first means this piece comes before the other

parts.note: St Luke, writer of a Gospel, is traditionally called the beloved physician
warm is hot in a milder sense

explanation.surface: Someone is unimpressed by a fervent preacher who is also a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot-gospeller' is an evangelical preacher, but the hyphen is split: 'hot' gives WARM and 'gospeller physician' is St Luke, placed first.
explanation.definitionFit: Lukewarm describes a tepid, half-hearted response.

clue.text: Mistake! Drinks noisily

indicators.note: noisily tells us to go by the sound of the drinking word, not its spelling

parts.note: a cat laps milk, drinking with its tongue

explanation.surface: Someone slurps drinks loudly, a social error.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a slip or small error, as in a lapse of concentration.

clue.text: Press argue, once reorganisation took place

indicators.note: a reorganisation means the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Journalists complained once the company was restructured.
explanation.definitionFit: To press someone to act is to urge or spur them on.

clue.text: Pass out for distressed guard needs a note

indicators.note: distressed means put into disorder, so the word guard is jumbled

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A guard in distress needs a note to be allowed out on parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass out' is military language for completing training, which is what a graduate does; GUARD jumbled gives GRADU.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass out of a training college is to finish the course and qualify, i.e. to complete one's studies.

clue.text: Weariness shown by eleven? Nuisance

indicators.note: shown by means the letters appear within the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: A tired eleven-strong team finds everything a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless boredom and world-weariness.

clue.text: A debt of gratitude got no alibi to fix

indicators.note: to fix means to rig or doctor, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A suspect without an alibi owes thanks to whoever fixes one.
explanation.definitionFit: An obligation is a duty one owes, here a moral debt.

clue.text: Newlywed almost came first, but showed annoyance

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a bride is a woman just married
to lead is to be in front, to come first

explanation.surface: A new bride nearly won a race but was cross about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To bridle is to bristle or toss the head in anger, like a reined horse.

clue.text: Cricket ground with joint title

parts.note: Lord's is the famous London cricket ground
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A peer receives a title at a cricket ground ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: LORD'S is the headquarters of English cricket in north London.
explanation.definitionFit: A lordship is the rank and form of address of a peer.

clue.text: Origins of the jam trade

definitions.meaning: what causes a jam on the roads is too many vehicles
as a verb or noun, to deal or barter, especially illicitly

explanation.definitionFit: Road congestion comes from vehicles in volume, and dealing in goods (drug dealing, arms) is also called by this word.

clue.text: Audience give a hand

definitions.meaning: a theatre with every seat taken
in poker, three of a kind plus a pair

explanation.definitionFit: A sold-out theatre and the poker holding of trips plus a pair share the same name.

clue.text: Takes no notice of Italian gentleman heading westwards

indicators.note: the heading, the first letter, is shifted along the word to the other end

parts.note: signore is the Italian for a gentleman or sir

explanation.surface: An Italian man walking west snubs everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore something is to pay no attention to it.

clue.text: Posed additional problem with a fruit

parts.note: a model sat or posed for a portrait
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: Someone set an extra puzzle involving a piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A satsuma is a small, easy-peeling citrus fruit like a mandarin.

clue.text: Good walk? Right, that's better

parts.note: an amble is a leisurely walk

explanation.surface: A pleasant stroll is described as an improvement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' looks like a comparative adjective but is a noun: one who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A punter who wagers money is a bettor, someone who stakes cash on outcomes.

clue.text: Good conundrum for how to cook?

parts.note: a riddle is a conundrum or puzzle

explanation.surface: A good puzzle about cooking methods.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook on a flat heated plate is one method of preparing food.

clue.text: Make collection for a service

parts.note: Mass is the Catholic church service of the Eucharist

explanation.surface: A collection plate is passed round at church.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather or accumulate a large quantity.

clue.text: Article on muscular contraction is a trick

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A twitch in a muscle is an illusion.
explanation.definitionFit: An antic is a playful caper or prank.

clue.text: Starts to wonder if answer comes before dark

indicators.note: starts means take the first letter of each of the next three words

parts.note: in crosswords a light is the answer filled in the grid

explanation.surface: Someone begins to wonder whether the solution will come before nightfall.
explanation.walkthrough: LIGHT is crossword jargon for a grid answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusk is the dim interval between sunset and full night.

clue.text: The whole house is absolutely freezing!

definitions.text: The whole house is absolutely freezing!

parts.words: The whole house is absolutely freezing!
parts.note: a complaint about a chilly home, read literally as a dwelling built entirely from ice

explanation.definitionFit: An Inuit snow dome is a home made of frozen blocks.

clue.text: Gamble, putting in a pound

indicators.note: putting in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a bet is a gamble

explanation.surface: Someone stakes a pound on a wager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' looks like money for the bet but is the definition, meaning thump.
explanation.definitionFit: To pound is to hit repeatedly, to strike hard.

clue.text: Puzzled, when United rig match

indicators.note: match here means fit together in a new arrangement, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Fans are baffled when Manchester United fix a football game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' looks like a football fixture but signals the anagram of UNITED and RIG.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrigued means curious and fascinated, puzzled in a pleasurable way.

clue.text: Look! Employ somebody who's worthless

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
to use is to employ

explanation.surface: Someone warns against hiring a good-for-nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A louse is a contemptible person, a scoundrel.

clue.text: Steal from prison

definitions.meaning: British slang for pinch or swipe
British slang for a jail or police station

explanation.definitionFit: Both pinching something and the jail you end up in go by the same British slang word.

clue.text: Spiteful chap editing novel before tea, say

parts.note: a chap is a man, a male

indicators.note: editing means the word novel is reworked into a new arrangement
say tells us to take the sound of the word tea, a single letter

parts.note: the drink tea sounds like the letter T

explanation.surface: A man revises his novel before taking his afternoon tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Malevolent means wishing harm on others, full of ill will.
